meta.purpose: One map from approved picture concept to older mnemonic concept to older art to files on disk, per letter. A test (tests/letters.artconcept.test.js) checks that the displayed fields in data/letters/mnemonics.json do not contradict it.

definitions.approved: the concept in data/letters/memory-chain.json; its SVG is in assets/letters/morph/
definitions.olderMnemonic: imageIdea, caption and story in data/letters/mnemonics.json
definitions.olderArt: the picture prompts in tools/images/spec.mjs and the files in assets/img/gen. The agreement judgments compare the prompt words only; no image was opened.
definitions.status: keep = nothing older conflicts; retire = an older concept conflicts, so its displayed text was rewritten (or never shown) and its art stays on disk, hidden; needs decision = a person must choose

meta.notDisplayed: altStory is shown only by the atlas "Another picture" button, which is hidden whenever the memory chain covers the letter (all 27). The nun-final and tsadi-final alt stories still mention a cat; they are listed here, not changed.
meta.olderArtHidden: Visibility is controlled per image by data/images/approvals.json; owner-approved older art may be shown
meta.stale: book/out, docs/workbook/html and the workbook PDFs were built before this pass and were not rebuilt

ayin.rule: Stated per reading, only from data/pronunciation/consonants.json (verified true): Israeli [ʔ] or silent, merged with alef ("do not try a pharyngeal in Israel"); Sephardi pharyngeal [ʕ] (Western Sephardim [ŋ]); Ashkenazi silent (relic [ŋ] in Yiddish Yankev, mayse).
fieldsChanged: mnemonics.json ayin sound, soundAnchor, story, altStory, caption, lookalike, imageIdea; alef lookalike; meta.note
tools/images/spec.mjs ayin sound (printed in the book header and the art prompt; it said "silent in Tel Aviv, throaty in Mizrahi speech", which the data does not say)
notDecidedByData: How many Sephardi or Mizrahi communities keep a throat sound for ayin, and which: the data gives one "Sephardi" textbook model and says it is not a model of any community.
Whether Ashkenazi ayin is always silent: data/traditions/sounds.json says "silent in most forms; traditional authorities advised a throaty sound in prayer, which is rarely done".
Aleph has the same issue: its fields say silent, while consonants.json lists a glottal stop [ʔ] for Sephardi. Not changed in this pass.

wordList.flags: needsReview: example token fits another entry; homograph

garden.segolHomograph: data/vocab/words.json also has the same consonants with segol + dagesh (id had0d3973, "a gene"); that is a different word.
garden.mnemonicsNow: patach + dagesh, copied from the word list
garden.reviewer: A qualified Hebrew reader should confirm the pointing and the word choice. The word list is dictionary-derived and flagged for review, and the data does not say whether the qamats form is a recognised variant, so it was not kept as one.

decisions: alef: keep the handstand mime (approved in the chain) or replace it with a Noa picture. The data shows no Noa letter picture.
Older art in assets/img/gen: keep hidden, rename or remove later. Nothing was deleted.
ayin and alef sound wording: reviewer to check the per-reading lines (see the ayin section).
garden pointing: reviewer to confirm patach + dagesh.
nun-final and tsadi-final alt stories still describe a cat: retire them or leave them hidden.

The brief mentions kneeling and standing nuns near lines 29 and 40 of mnemonics.json. Those lines are the nun (napping cat) and nun-final (nail) records; no kneeling or standing nun text was found in the file. docs/DECISIONS-NEEDED.md item 13 says a kneeling-nun picture was already replaced by the cat.
